compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: Jesus says he came not to destroy Law or Prophets but fulfill, speaks of enduring detail, practice and teaching, and righteousness beyond scribes and Pharisees.
observations.label: Jesus speaks of fulfillment, endurance, practice, and righteousness

observations.body: Jesus speaks of fulfillment, endurance, practice, and righteousness belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Matthew 5:17–20 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.

payload.posture: Read Matthew 5:17–20 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Jesus speaks of fulfillment, endurance, practice, and righteousness belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
